action: At pinned modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk commit 4a738b9dd99eaca418b614afa433a0cbdaf8d056, inspect RequestMetaObject, ProtocolVersion, ClientCapabilities, and Streamable HTTP pre-dispatch validation to determine whether well-typed per-request protocolVersion/clientCapabilities values that differ from previously initialized peer context are rejected before dispatch.
result: RequestMetaObject is a transparent JSON object wrapper. protocol_version() and client_capabilities() decode their reserved values lazily, while missing_required_keys() checks only that the values decode to ProtocolVersion and ClientCapabilities for 2026-07-28 metadata requirements. ProtocolVersion deserialization accepts every JSON string: known strings map to constants and any other string becomes an owned ProtocolVersion. ClientCapabilities derives ordinary Serde deserialization with optional fields and no deny_unknown_fields marker, so a different structurally valid capabilities object decodes successfully. In Streamable HTTP, validate_request_protocol_version_meta requires a per-request protocolVersion to have a matching MCP-Protocol-Version header, and modern/discover paths may require the metadata to be well-typed, but the validator does not compare protocolVersion or clientCapabilities to previously initialized peer_info. A request carrying per-request protocol metadata is routed through serve_negotiated_request_directly in the stateless/per-request path; peer_info for that dispatch is reconstructed from the same request header, not from an earlier handshake. Therefore decode/structural validation does not itself enforce equality with initialized peer context: a supported-but-different protocolVersion can pass when its request header matches, and a different structurally valid clientCapabilities object is not rejected for differing from prior capabilities. For generic non-HTTP serve_inner, the prior slice already found no peer_info consistency gate after decoding; for Streamable HTTP, metadata-bearing requests may be rerouted to direct per-request dispatch rather than the prior session's generic serve_inner.
